source_text.Q-1058: CI main flake / defect, HIGH. Property 'any set of row writers is invisible after the boundary, and never rebuilds' in test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs (property ~L1402, failing assertion ~L1430 `assert nonseed_rows(a.schema_name) == []`) fails on some ExUnit seeds. Regression of Q-1042 (PR #2397, edf3e614). Evidence: reproduced locally with `LETFLOW_DB_PORT=5499 MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs --seed 193355` => 56/57; failing case after 2 successful runs: writers [:groups], via :test; nonseed_rows(a.schema_name) got [{"groups",1}] after recycle_pool! although pool_dirty_report(fx(:a)) said clean. Second occurrence on main 28fcc928, CI run 38235738863, shard 3/3 partition 11, seed 40898. H1 (isolation hole, the worse case): the pool leaves a row in an attached tenant after recycle, so a later test can see another test's writes. H2 (test defect): the property asserts on a.schema_name after a recycle that attached a different slot, so it checks the wrong schema. Acceptance: (1) root cause H1 or H2 with evidence from seeds 193355 and 40898 quoted; (2) if H1: SECURITY-REVIEWER note, the hole fixed, fix shown to hold on the failing sequences; (3) if H2: the assertion checks the schema that holds the writes, decision recorded with reasoning; (4) both seeds added as fixed regression cases of the property; (5) the property passes on the failing seeds and on a fresh sample of seeds across consecutive runs, real output quoted; (6) the property's claim (writers invisible after the boundary, no rebuild) is NOT weakened. Related, not duplicates: ISS-1054 (R1 current_database guard), ISS-1055 (R5 typing), ISS-1056 (V2 depth-2 FK). GH #2406, Q-1058.

result.summary: Design lib/letflow/design/iss1058-pool-property-claims-leak.md covers all 6 acceptance criteria; every factual claim re-verified against test/support/tenant_fixture.ex and test/letflow/support/tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs by direct reading; no implementation code; no lib/ or test/support change; claim not weakened. No BLOCKER, no MAJOR; 3 MINOR findings, none gating.
verified: F1-F3: @claims_key L297; claim_pooled! L589-598 takes k=Map.get(claims,shape,0), puts k+1 at L596, ArgumentError for undeclared slot L600-607; recycle_pool! L493-497 clears claims at L495 then run_end_fence!, touches no data.

F4: reset is lazy, at do_acquire (L1702): fence_a! -> prove_clean -> final_guard!; the other slot is untouched. F5: {:dirty_report, schema_name} (L1393) resolves slot by schema_name only. F6: attach_pool! L462 refuses non-empty claims.
Test side: slots [@a,@a,@b] L46-53; fx(:a) L98; property body ~L1402-1435 as described, max_runs 12, generators as described, closing rebuilds equality.

:fk_chain is the ONLY fixed-PK writer in @prop_writers: write!(:fk_chain) L246-274 uses literals ...0a1/...0b1 in groups/users/group_members/tenant_role. All other 9 writers use gen_random_uuid() or uniq() (names, emails, module_id, correlation_id; events instance_id random so (instance_id,sequence_number) never collides; seq_only writes no row). grep of the two literals in test/ and lib/ hits only tenant_fixture_pool_test.exs. Fixed-case users (mutate_everything! L413, M1 L528, M11 L1142) call it once per slot after an acquire that reset the slot, so unaffected.

Recycle at iteration start is sound: it only clears the per-process counter and runs the straggler fence; no slot data is touched, dirt is reset lazily by the next acquire of that slot regardless; the boundary under test (write, recycle, acquire) is outside it.

Pinned cases C1/C1b/C2/C3 encode the failing chain from the ISS-1058 diagnosis (duplicate :fk_chain -> 23505 -> claims {a=>1} leaks -> shrink re-run claims slot 2 -> post-boundary slot 1; seed 40898 second leak -> ArgumentError {shape,2}). Hand-traced C3: abort_attempt! x2 leaves claims {a=>2}; without change 2 helper fx(:a) raises ArgumentError, with it the start recycle yields slot 1 and the dirty slots are reset at acquire. Seeds themselves cannot be pinned through ExUnit; design O4 records that and encodes sequences instead (acceptable reading of acceptance 4).
Hooks hook_after_verify/hook_after_guard are no-ops unless a test sets the persistent_term (none do in the property); no hidden masking from them.

mutant_verification.MU1: EXISTS and FAILS the property, not masked by a rebuild. prove_clean (L1740-1763) else-arm at L1759-1761 calls reset/4. Replacing it by {state,:clean} touches neither the rebuild branches (probe error / definition drift only) nor final_guard!. Next acquire of the dirty slot: final_guard! L1862 probes with probe_clone_data, sees dirty tables, attempt 1 -> bump final_guard_resets, add_fallback(:final_guard), prove_clean again (still mutated, no reset), attempt 2 -> fail() throw -> ExUnit.AssertionError at fx(:a), message reason=pool_straggler "written to again after two resets". No rebuild occurs (rebuild/4 is only reachable from detect error, drift, or public-verify failure), so the end-of-property rebuilds equality is not what catches it. It fails at the post-boundary fx(:a) of the SAME iteration (or the next iteration start-acquire).
mutant_verification.MU2: EXISTS (reset/4 L1765-1810, reset_clone_schema! call L1769-1772) and FAILS the property. Stub {:ok, report} needs fields truncated, closure_added, sequences_restarted, probe_ms, verify_ms, total_ms (all read at L1779-1789) - design lists them. public_clean?(public_state) holds because the writers only write the tenant schema, so :reset is reported; rows and sequence state stay; final_guard! attempt 1 -> prove_clean -> same stub -> attempt 2 -> fail, identical observable outcome to MU1. No rebuild masking.
mutant_verification.MU3: EXISTS (L495) and FAILS at the new same-schema assertion on the first iteration: claims not cleared, post-boundary fx(:a) claims slot 2, a.schema_name != again.schema_name. (attach_pool! L468 also clears claims but runs once in setup, so it does not mask.) Correct as designed.
mutant_verification.caveat: Under MU1/MU2 the property fails at final_guard!, which subsumes the property assertions at ~L1430-1431: probe_clone_data + clean_diff? (tenant_template.ex L612) cover dirty_tables AND dirty_sequences. So the design statement that MU2 "proves the row/sequence assertions at L1430-1431 still carry weight and are not subsumed by the pool report" is not true; those assertions are reachable only by a mutant that also blinds the guard/detect (for example diff_clone_state or clean_diff? always clean), and are otherwise defence in depth. See finding m1.

findings.text: Section 7 MU1/MU2 rationale overstated: failure surfaces through final_guard! (pool_straggler, after two attempts), never at nonseed_rows/called_sequences; the "if the guard passes" arm is unreachable. TEST-RUNNER/TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR should expect and record the guard message as the observed failing assertion for MU1/MU2 (the design already lists "the guard" first, so it is within expectation). If proof that L1430-1431 carry independent weight is wanted, add MU4 that blinds clean_diff?/diff_clone_state; not required for the property to be shown non-weakened.
Line cite for prove_clean is L1740-1763 (else-arm reset call L1759-1761), design says L1740-1759. Cosmetic; mutation target is unambiguous.

Acceptance 4 "both seeds added as fixed regression cases" is met by encoding the failing sequences (C1-C3), not by a literal seed pin; justified in O4 (ExUnit --seed is not a property parameter). TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR should accept that reading and require the --seed 193355 and --seed 40898 whole-file runs as corroboration, as design section 6 states.
